scope: Deferred reverse release must retain its exact cap baseline
finding: DrivingRecoveryRelease can return false with an exact releasePending reverse journal while immobile/simulation unavailable, but DrivingAssistRelease ignored that result and restored/cleared its speed-cap state anyway.
implementation: After recovery release, retain cap/restoration state only for an unretired releasePending journal still exactly equal to the current public work. Retired/replaced/non-pending work follows existing cleanup and exact newer-controller cap guards. No deadline renewal or observer.

investigated_not_changed.subject: Driving current-waypoint count validation
investigated_not_changed.result: Official documentation explicitly describes comparing currentWaypoint with waypoint count. No speculative hole/index fix was made; existing guards were not treated as a confirmed fault.

remaining: Whole-subsystem shutdown has no guaranteed deferred-handback observation path.
Physical repair/simulation recovery, repeat release, new external caps and migration acceptance.
Same-value external speed writes cannot be attributed without cooperation.
No whole-feature or runtime performance acceptance.
